sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for the applicants states that he does not want to press the prayer for quashing of the impugned order.

He states that the purpose of the applicants would be served if they are permitted to appear before the subordinate court within a period of two weeks from today and file a regular bail application but till then the non-bailable warrants as issued may be kept in abeyance.
It is argued that non-bailable warrants have been issued vide order dated 23.11.2021 passed by the trial court.
5. Learned counsel for the State has no objection of aforesaid arguments of learned counsel for the applicants.
6. In view of the above, the prayer for quashing of impugned order is dismissed as not pressed.

7. However, in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the limited prayer of learned counsel for the applicants, it is directed that if the accused-applicants appear and apply for bail before the court concerned within two weeks from today, the same shall be considered and decided in accordance with law.
Till the aforesaid period, the non-bailable warrants shall be kept in abeyance.
8. It it clarified that if the accused-applicants do not appear before the court concerned by the said date, the court concerned shall proceed against them in accordance with law.
9. The present application is disposed of.
